56. // Inner
57. //==================================================================================================
58. 
59. /// BSS-backed per-frame reference count storage. Indexed by frame number.
60. ///
61. /// Sits in BSS rather than on the kernel heap because the slab allocator caps single
62. /// allocations at a few hundred bytes, but a full refcount table for the configured
63. /// memory size is much larger.
64. ///
65. /// # Size impact
66. ///
67. /// This array is unconditionally reserved in BSS and scales linearly with the
68. /// configured machine memory size: `MEMORY_SIZE / FRAME_SIZE * size_of::<u8>()`
69. /// bytes (e.g. 256 KiB for a 1 GiB configuration). A `u8` is sufficient because at
70. /// most [`config::kernel::MAX_PROCESSES`] (≤ 255) processes can simultaneously share a
71. /// frame, so the refcount of any frame is bounded by 255.
72. ///
73. /// # Safety
74. ///
75. /// Accessed only through `Inner::refcount`, which is set up at boot from this storage
76. /// and never aliased. The kernel is single-threaded and runs with interrupts disabled,
77. /// so non-atomic access is sound.
78. static mut REFCOUNT_STORAGE: [u8; NFRAMES] = [0; NFRAMES];
79. 
80. /// Private state of the frame allocator singleton.
81. #[verus_verify]
82. struct Inner {
83.     /// A bitmap that keeps track of free/used frames.
84.     bitmap: Bitmap,
85.     /// Per-frame reference count. Indexed by frame number.
86.     ///
87.     /// Invariants:
88.     ///
89.     /// - `refcount.len() >= bitmap.number_of_bits()`.
90.     /// - `refcount[i] >= 1` iff bit `i` is set in `bitmap` (for `i < bitmap.number_of_bits()`).
91.     /// - `refcount[i] == 0` iff bit `i` is clear in `bitmap` (for `i < bitmap.number_of_bits()`).
92.     ///
93.     /// A refcount greater than one means that the frame is shared between multiple
94.     /// owners (e.g. parent and child after [`share`]). The frame is reclaimed (bitmap
95.     /// bit cleared) only when the refcount reaches zero.
96.     ///
97.     /// The element type is `u8`: the kernel caps the number of live processes at
98.     /// [`config::kernel::MAX_PROCESSES`] (≤ 255), so a frame can be shared by at most 255
99.     /// owners and the count always fits in a byte.
100.     refcount: &'static mut [u8],
101. }
102. 
103. #[verus_verify]
104. impl Inner {
105.     ///
106.     /// # Description
107.     ///
108.     /// Allocates a frame.
109.     ///
110.     /// # Returns
111.     ///
112.     /// Upon success, the address of the allocated frame is returned. Upon failure, an error is
113.     /// returned instead.
114.     ///
115.     #[verus_spec(result =>
116.         requires
117.             old(self).inv(),
118.         ensures
119.             final(self).inv(),
120.             match result {

340.     /// This is used to implement page sharing (e.g. for copy-on-write). The matching
341.     /// number of [`free`] calls must be issued to actually release the frame back to
342.     /// the bitmap.
343.     ///
344.     /// # Parameters
345.     ///
346.     /// - `frame`: Address of the frame to share.
347.     ///
348.     /// # Returns
349.     ///
350.     /// Upon success, `Ok(())` is returned. Upon failure, an error is returned instead.
351.     ///
352.     #[verus_spec(result =>
353.         requires
354.             old(self).inv(),
355.             frame.inv(),
356.         ensures
357.             final(self).inv(),
358.             match result {
359.                 Ok(()) => {
360.                     &&& old(self)@.allocated_frames.contains(frame@)
361.                     &&& old(self)@.refcounts.contains_key(frame@)
362.                     &&& final(self)@ == FrameAllocView {
363.                         allocated_frames: old(self)@.allocated_frames,
364.                         free_frames: old(self)@.free_frames,
365.                         refcounts: old(self)@.refcounts.insert(
366.                             frame@, old(self)@.refcounts[frame@] + 1
367.                         ),
368.                     }
369.                 },
370.                 Err(_) => {
371.                     &&& final(self)@ == old(self)@
372.                     &&& (
373.                         !old(self)@.allocated_frames.contains(frame@)
374.                         || (old(self)@.refcounts.contains_key(frame@)
375.                             && old(self)@.refcounts[frame@] >= 255)
376.                     )
377.                 }
378.             },
379.     )]
380.     fn share(&mut self, frame: FrameAddress) -> Result<(), Error> {
381.         // VERUS BUG FIX: avoid into_frame_number()'s panicking unwrap on the top-of-space
382.         // aligned address; compute the index totally (downstream bounds checks reject oversized).
383.         let frame_number: usize = frame.into_raw_value() / mem::FRAME_SIZE;
384. 
385.         if frame_number >= self.refcount.len() {
386.             let reason: &str = "frame number out of bounds";
387.             #[cfg(not(verus_keep_ghost))]
388.             error!("{reason} (frame={frame:?})");
389.             return Err(Error::new(ErrorCode::BadAddress, reason));
390.         }
391. 
392.         // The frame must currently have at least one owner. Sharing an unallocated
393.         // frame is a logic error.
394.         if self.refcount[frame_number] == 0 {
395.             let reason: &str = "cannot share an unallocated frame";
396.             #[cfg(not(verus_keep_ghost))]
397.             error!("{reason} (frame={frame:?})");
398.             return Err(Error::new(ErrorCode::BadAddress, reason));
399.         }
400. 
401.         self.refcount[frame_number] = match self.refcount[frame_number].checked_add(1) {
402.             Some(n) => n,
403.             None => {
404.                 let reason: &str = "frame reference count overflow";
405.                 #[cfg(not(verus_keep_ghost))]
406.                 error!("{reason} (frame={frame:?})");
407.                 return Err(Error::new(ErrorCode::OutOfMemory, reason));
408.             },
409.         };
410. 
411.         Ok(())
412.     }
413. 
414.     ///
415.     /// # Description
416.     ///
417.     /// Returns the current reference count of an already-allocated frame.
418.     ///
419.     /// # Parameters
420.     ///
421.     /// - `frame`: Address of the frame to query.
422.     ///
423.     /// # Returns
424.     ///
425.     /// Upon success, the current reference count is returned. Upon failure, an error is
426.     /// returned instead (out-of-bounds address, or the frame is not currently allocated).
427.     ///
428.     #[verus_spec(result =>
429.         requires
430.             self.inv(),
431.         ensures
432.             self.inv(),
433.             match result {
434.                 Ok(count) => {
435.                     &&& self@.allocated_frames.contains(frame@)
436.                     &&& self@.refcounts.contains_key(frame@)
437.                     &&& count as int == self@.refcounts[frame@]
438.                 },
439.                 Err(_) => {
440.                     !self@.allocated_frames.contains(frame@)
441.                 }
442.             },
443.     )]
444.     fn refcount(&self, frame: FrameAddress) -> Result<u8, Error> {
445.         // VERUS BUG FIX: avoid into_frame_number()'s panicking unwrap on the top-of-space
446.         // aligned address; compute the index totally (downstream bounds checks reject oversized).
447.         let frame_number: usize = frame.into_raw_value() / mem::FRAME_SIZE;
448. 
449.         if frame_number >= self.refcount.len() {
450.             let reason: &str = "frame number out of bounds";
451.             #[cfg(not(verus_keep_ghost))]
452.             error!("{reason} (frame={frame:?})");
453.             return Err(Error::new(ErrorCode::BadAddress, reason));
454.         }
455. 
456.         if self.refcount[frame_number] == 0 {
457.             let reason: &str = "frame is not allocated";
458.             #[cfg(not(verus_keep_ghost))]
459.             error!("{reason} (frame={frame:?})");
460.             return Err(Error::new(ErrorCode::BadAddress, reason));
461.         }
462. 
463.         Ok(self.refcount[frame_number])
464.     }
465. 
466.     ///
467.     /// # Description
468.     ///
469.     /// Books a frame so that it will not be handed out by [`alloc`].
470.     ///
471.     /// # Parameters
472.     ///
473.     /// - `phys_addr`: Physical address of the frame to book.
474.     ///
475.     /// # Returns
476.     ///
477.     /// Upon success, `Ok(())` is returned. Upon failure, an error is returned instead.
478.     ///
479.     #[verus_spec(result =>
480.         requires
481.             old(self).inv(),
482.             phys_addr.inv(),
483.         ensures
484.             final(self).inv(),
485.             match result {
486.                 Ok(()) => {
487.                     &&& old(self)@.free_frames.contains(phys_addr@)
488.                     &&& final(self)@ == FrameAllocView {
489.                         allocated_frames: old(self)@.allocated_frames.insert(phys_addr@),
490.                         free_frames: old(self)@.free_frames.remove(phys_addr@),
491.                         refcounts: old(self)@.refcounts.insert(phys_addr@, 1int),
492.                     }
493.                 },
494.                 Err(_) => {
495.                     &&& final(self)@ == old(self)@
496.                     &&& !old(self)@.free_frames.contains(phys_addr@)
497.                 }
498.             },
499.     )]
500.     fn book(&mut self, phys_addr: PageAligned<PhysicalAddress>) -> Result<(), Error> {
501.         // VERUS BUG FIX: avoid into_frame_number()'s panicking unwrap on the top-of-space
502.         // aligned address; compute the index totally (bitmap.set rejects oversized indices).
503.         let frame_number: usize = phys_addr.into_raw_value() / mem::FRAME_SIZE;
504.         match self.bitmap.set(frame_number) {
505.             Ok(()) => {
506.                 #[cfg(not(verus_keep_ghost))]
507.                 debug_assert_eq!(self.refcount[frame_number], 0);
508.                 self.refcount[frame_number] = 1;
509.                 Ok(())
510.             },
511.             Err(error) => {
512.                 #[cfg(not(verus_keep_ghost))]
513.                 error!("{error:?} (phys_addr={phys_addr:?})");
514.                 Err(error)
515.             },
516.         }
517.     }
518. 
519.     ///
520.     /// # Description
521.     ///
522.     /// Checks whether the frame allocator tracks the frame at the given physical address.
523.     ///
524.     /// # Returns
525.     ///
526.     /// `true` if the frame allocator tracks the frame at `phys_addr`, `false` otherwise.
527.     ///
528.     #[verus_spec(ret =>
529.         requires
530.             self.inv(),
531.             phys_addr.inv(),
532.         ensures
533.             self.inv(),
534.             ret <==> (
535.                 self@.allocated_frames.contains(phys_addr@)
536.                 || self@.free_frames.contains(phys_addr@)
537.             ),
538.     )]
539.     fn is_covered(&self, phys_addr: PageAligned<PhysicalAddress>) -> bool {
540.         // VERUS BUG FIX: avoid into_frame_number()'s panicking unwrap on the top-of-space
541.         // aligned address; compute the index totally (compared against num_bits below).
542.         let frame_number: usize = phys_addr.into_raw_value() / mem::FRAME_SIZE;
543.         frame_number < self.bitmap.number_of_bits()
544.     }
545. 
546.     ///
547.     /// # Description
548.     ///
549.     /// Allocates all frames in the given region.
550.     ///
551.     /// # Parameters
552.     ///
553.     /// - `region`: Physical memory region whose frames should be booked.
554.     ///
555.     /// # Returns
556.     ///
557.     /// Upon success, `Ok(())` is returned. Upon failure, an error is returned instead.
558.     ///
559.     #[verus_spec(result =>
560.         requires

720. pub(super) unsafe fn init(bitmap: Bitmap) -> Result<(), Error> {
721.     if unlikely(INSTANCE_INIT.load(ORDER)) {
722.         return Err(Error::new(ErrorCode::InvalidArgument, "frame allocator already initialized"));
723.     }
724. 
725.     info!(
726.         "frame allocator: {} frames, {} MB",
727.         bitmap.number_of_bits(),
728.         (bitmap.number_of_bits() * mem::FRAME_SIZE) / constants::MEGABYTE,
729.     );
730. 
731.     let nframes: usize = bitmap.number_of_bits();
732.     if nframes > NFRAMES {
733.         return Err(Error::new(
734.             ErrorCode::InvalidArgument,
735.             "frame bitmap is larger than the configured refcount storage",
736.         ));
737.     }
738. 
739.     // SAFETY: single-threaded boot; no other reference to `REFCOUNT_STORAGE` exists.
740.     let refcount: &'static mut [u8] = unsafe { &mut REFCOUNT_STORAGE[..] };
741. 
742.     // Defensively sync refcounts with any bits already set in the incoming bitmap. The
743.     // current microvm boot path supplies an empty bitmap and performs all reservations
744.     // via `book()` / `alloc_range()` after `init()`, so this loop normally does nothing.
745.     // It is kept as a safety net so a future boot path that hands us a pre-populated
746.     // bitmap (for example to express firmware-reserved regions) does not silently end
747.     // up with `bitmap bit = 1, refcount = 0`, which would cause the first `free()` of
748.     // such a frame to be rejected as a spurious double-free.
749.     for (i, slot) in refcount.iter_mut().enumerate().take(nframes) {
750.         if matches!(bitmap.test(i), Ok(true)) {
751.             *slot = 1;
752.         }
753.     }
754. 
755.     // SAFETY: single-threaded boot; no other reference to `INSTANCE` exists.
756.     unsafe { INSTANCE.write(Inner { bitmap, refcount }) };
757.     INSTANCE_INIT.store(true, ORDER);
758.     Ok(())
759. }
760. 
761. /// Allocate a frame.
762. // Dependency contract for the manager layer: thin singleton wrapper around `Inner::alloc`.
763. // `external_body` until the `frame` free-function layer is verified; the manager bridges the
764. // returned address into its own abstract frame partition via a proof lemma.
765. #[verus_verify(external_body)]
766. #[verus_spec(result =>
767.     ensures
768.         match result {
769.             Ok(frame) => {
770.                 &&& frame.inv()
771.                 &&& crate::mm::phys::phys_view().frames.allocated_frames.contains(frame@)
772.             },
773.             Err(_) => crate::mm::phys::phys_view().frames.free_frames.is_empty(),
774.         },
775. )]
776. pub(super) fn alloc() -> Result<FrameAddress, Error> {
777.     instance().alloc()
778. }
779. 
780. /// # Description
781. ///
782. /// Allocates `count` physically contiguous frames.
783. ///
784. /// # Returns
785. ///
786. /// Returns the base `FrameAddress` of the contiguous range.
787. ///
788. // Dependency contract: thin singleton wrapper around `Inner::alloc_contiguous`. The base
789. // address is page-aligned on success. The address-space range bound (`base@ + count*PS <=
790. // usize::MAX`) is the fact the manager's per-frame index arithmetic relies upon; it follows
791. // from `Inner::alloc_contiguous`'s frame-set postcondition plus the allocator invariant
792. // (bridged in the proving phase).
793. #[verus_verify(external_body)]
794. #[verus_spec(result =>
795.     requires
796.         count > 0,
797.     ensures
798.         match result {
799.             Ok(base) => {
800.                 &&& base.inv()
801.                 &&& base@ + (count as int) * spec_page_size() <= usize::MAX as int
802.             },
803.             Err(_) => true,
804.         },
805. )]
806. pub(super) fn alloc_contiguous(count: usize) -> Result<FrameAddress, Error> {
807.     instance().alloc_contiguous(count)
808. }
809. 
810. ///
811. /// # Description
812. ///
813. /// Returns the number of free frames in the system.
814. ///
815. /// # Returns
816. ///
817. /// The number of free frames in the system.
818. ///
819. // Dependency contract: reports the size of the free partition of the global frame allocator.
820. // The bitmap-level count (`number_of_bits - usage`) equals the abstract `free_count()`
821. // (`free_frames.len()`); this is bridged in the proving phase.
822. #[verus_verify(external_body)]
823. #[verus_spec(result =>
824.     ensures
825.         result as nat == crate::mm::phys::phys_view().frames.free_count(),
826. )]
827. pub(super) fn free_count() -> usize {
828.     let inner = instance();
829.     inner.bitmap.number_of_bits() - inner.bitmap.usage()
830. }
831. 
832. /// Free a frame previously returned by [`alloc`].
833. // Dependency contract: best-effort release of a frame. Callers (the manager's error-cleanup
834. // paths and the `Drop` impls) ignore the outcome, so no precondition is imposed and no abstract
835. // postcondition is promised. `opens_invariants none`/`no_unwind` so it is callable from
836. // `UserFrame::drop`/`KernelFrame::drop`. The underlying `Inner::free` precondition (`frame.inv()`)
837. // is discharged in the proving phase from the `FrameAddress` type invariant.
838. #[verus_verify(external_body)]
839. #[verus_spec(result =>
840.     ensures
841.         true,
842.     opens_invariants none
843.     no_unwind
844. )]
845. pub(super) fn free(frame: FrameAddress) -> Result<(), Error> {
846.     instance().free(frame)
847. }
848. 
849. ///
850. /// # Description
851. ///
852. /// Checks whether the frame allocator tracks the frame at the given physical address.
853. ///
854. /// # Returns
855. ///
856. /// Returns `true` when the frame allocator tracks the frame at `phys_addr`.
857. ///
858. // Dependency contract: pure coverage query over the global frame partition. `true` iff the
859. // allocator tracks the frame (allocated or free), i.e. `phys_view().frames.covers(phys_addr@)`.
860. // Used by the MMIO boot path to skip frames above RAM that the bitmap does not cover.
861. #[verus_spec(ret =>
862.     requires
863.         phys_addr.inv(),
864.     ensures
865.         ret <==> crate::mm::phys::phys_view().frames.covers(phys_addr@),
866. )]
867. pub(super) fn is_covered(phys_addr: PageAligned<PhysicalAddress>) -> bool {
868.     instance().is_covered(phys_addr)
869. }
870. 
871. /// Reserve a frame so [`alloc`] will skip it.
872. // Dependency contract: singleton wrapper around `Inner::book`. Reserves a covered, previously
873. // free frame (refcount becomes 1) so `alloc` never hands it out. The per-frame reservation is
874. // recorded in the global partition; the booking transition lives in `Inner::book` and is bridged
875. // to `phys_view().frames` in the proving phase. The boot caller (`book_mmio_regions`) re-derives
876. // the region-level booking facts via its own lemmas.
877. #[verus_verify(external_body)]
878. #[verus_spec(result =>
879.     requires
880.         phys_addr.inv(),
881.     ensures
882.         match result {
883.             Ok(()) => crate::mm::phys::phys_view().frames.reserved(phys_addr@),
884.             Err(_) => !crate::mm::phys::phys_view().frames.free_frames.contains(phys_addr@),
885.         },
886. )]
887. pub(super) fn book(phys_addr: PageAligned<PhysicalAddress>) -> Result<(), Error> {
888.     instance().book(phys_addr)
889. }
890. 
891. /// Book every frame in the given physical memory region.
892. // Dependency contract: singleton wrapper around `Inner::alloc_range`. On success every frame in
893. // the region (which must all be free) is reserved with refcount 1. The region-level transition
894. // lives in `Inner::alloc_range`; the boot caller (`book_physical_memory_regions`) re-derives the
895. // region-set booking facts via its own lemmas.
896. #[verus_verify(external_body)]
897. #[verus_spec(result =>
898.     requires
899.         region.inv(),
900.     ensures
901.         match result {
902.             Ok(()) => crate::mm::phys::phys_view().frames.all_reserved(
903.                 crate::mm::phys::region_frame_addrs(region@.start, region@.size)),
904.             Err(_) => !crate::mm::phys::phys_view().frames.all_free(
905.                 crate::mm::phys::region_frame_addrs(region@.start, region@.size)),
906.         },
907. )]
908. pub(super) fn alloc_range(region: &TruncatedMemoryRegion<PhysicalAddress>) -> Result<(), Error> {
909.     instance().alloc_range(region)
910. }
911. 
912. /// Add a new reference to an already-allocated frame (e.g. for copy-on-write sharing).
913. // Dependency contract: singleton wrapper around `Inner::share`. On success the frame is (still)
914. // allocated; the per-frame reference-count increment lives in the global partition and is pinned
915. // to `phys_view().frames` in the proving phase. `external_body` until the free-function layer is
916. // verified.
917. #[verus_verify(external_body)]
918. #[verus_spec(result =>
919.     requires
920.         frame.inv(),
921.     ensures
922.         match result {
923.             Ok(()) => crate::mm::phys::phys_view().frames.allocated_frames.contains(frame@),
924.             Err(_) => !crate::mm::phys::phys_view().frames.allocated_frames.contains(frame@)
925.                 || crate::mm::phys::phys_view().frames.refcounts[frame@] >= 255,
926.         },
927. )]
928. pub(super) fn share(frame: FrameAddress) -> Result<(), Error> {
929.     instance().share(frame)
930. }
931. 
932. /// Returns the current reference count of an already-allocated frame.
933. // Dependency contract: singleton wrapper around `Inner::refcount`. Reads the current reference
934. // count of the frame from the global partition (`phys_view().frames`); pure, no mutation.
935. // `external_body` until the free-function layer is verified.
936. #[verus_verify(external_body)]
937. #[verus_spec(result =>
938.     requires
939.         frame.inv(),
940.     ensures
941.         match result {
942.             Ok(count) => {
943.                 &&& crate::mm::phys::phys_view().frames.allocated_frames.contains(frame@)
944.                 &&& count as int == crate::mm::phys::phys_view().frames.refcounts[frame@]
945.             },
946.             Err(_) => !crate::mm::phys::phys_view().frames.allocated_frames.contains(frame@),
947.         },
948. )]
949. pub(super) fn refcount(frame: FrameAddress) -> Result<u8, Error> {
950.     instance().refcount(frame)
951. }

# Bugs / Suspicious code — `mm::phys::frame`

## [open] `Inner::alloc_range`: possible off-by-one between body and spec

- Body (frame.rs:588-589, 598, 626):
  - `start_frame_number = region.start().into_frame_number().into_raw_value()`
  - `end_frame_number = start_frame_number + region.size() / mem::FRAME_SIZE - 1`
  - loops are inclusive: `for index in start_frame_number..=end_frame_number`
- Spec (frame.rs:561-564):
  - `start_frame_number = region@.start / spec_page_size()`
  - `end_frame_number = (region@.start + region@.size) / spec_page_size()` (exclusive)
  - `frame_numbers = set_int_range(start, end)` (half-open `[start, end)`)

The body's inclusive `..=(start + size/FS - 1)` covers frames
`start .. start + size/FS`, i.e. `size/FS` frames. The spec's half-open range covers
`(start+size)/FS - start/FS` frames. These coincide only when both `region@.start`
and `region@.size` are exact multiples of `FRAME_SIZE` (so integer division does not
truncate). `region.inv()` presumably guarantees page-alignment of `start`; the `size`
multiple-of-FRAME_SIZE assumption must be confirmed, otherwise the booked set differs
from the spec'd set by one frame.

Currently masked by `proof! { admit(); }` at the top of `alloc_range`. The proving
phase must confirm `region.inv() ==> region@.start % page_size == 0 && region@.size %
page_size == 0` (or adjust the spec/body) before removing the admit.

Status: to confirm in proving phase. Raised during specification-phase review (turn 1).

## [auto-fixed] panic-on-valid-input: `into_frame_number().unwrap()` on top-of-space aligned address

**Where**: `Inner::free` (frame.rs:300), `Inner::share` (:381), `Inner::refcount` (:444),
`Inner::book` (:499), `Inner::is_covered` (:536), `Inner::alloc_range` (:587).

**What**: Each method converted an input address to a frame index via
`X.into_frame_number().into_raw_value()`. `PhysicalAddress/FrameAddress::into_frame_number`
is a *checked* conversion: internally `FrameNumber::from_raw_value(addr >> FRAME_SHIFT).unwrap()`,
which **panics** when the frame number exceeds `FrameNumber::MAX = MAX_ADDRESS/FRAME_SIZE - 1`.

**Why**: With `MAX_ADDRESS == usize::MAX`, the single page-aligned address
`usize::MAX - 4095` maps to frame `usize::MAX/4096 = FrameNumber::MAX + 1`, which arch
deliberately excludes (the top frame's end address `base + FRAME_SIZE` would overflow `usize`).
The method preconditions only guarantee page-alignment (`frame.inv()` / `phys_addr.inv()`),
which does **not** rule out this address. So a caller passing the top-of-space aligned address
